instrument_name: CDLE COMPS Order #40 Poster & Notice (Colorado Overtime & Minimum Pay Standards), effective 1/1/2026
authority: Colorado Department of Labor and Employment (CDLE), Division of Labor Standards and Statistics
article_or_section: COMPS Order #40 (7 CCR 1103-1) Rules 1.9, 2.2-2.4, 3, 4, 5.1, 5.2, 6, 7, 8 as summarised on the official poster
figure_or_rule_carried: State minimum wage 15.16 USD/h in 2026 (Rule 3), updated yearly; highest applicable (local) minimum wage applies; unemancipated minors may be paid 15% less (not for some local minimum wages); tip credit up to 3.02 USD/h (tipped cash wage 12.14 derived); overtime 1.5x regular rate after 40 hours/week, or 12 hours/day or 12 consecutive hours (Rule 4); no comp time in lieu of overtime; agriculture overtime after 48 hours (56 at some highly seasonal sites); EAP exemption salary 57,784 USD (updated yearly); meal period 30 min after shifts over 5 h; paid 10-min rest per 4 hours; pay statements must show total pay, rate, tips, credits and time worked, kept 3 years; final pay promptly on employer termination or next pay date on resignation; unused vacation must be paid to departing employees even if fired for cause; lodging credit 25-100 USD weekly; deductions only per CRS 8-4-105.

instrument_name: Colorado Wage Act C.R.S. 8-4-103(1) pay periods/paydays; 8-4-102(2),(2.5) direct deposit and paycard; 8-4-107 payday notice
authority: Colorado General Assembly (text published by CDLE)
figure_or_rule_carried: Wages due for regular pay periods no longer than one calendar month or 30 days (whichever longer), paid on regular paydays no later than 10 days after the close of the period, unless employer and employee agree otherwise (8-4-103(1)(a)). Direct deposit only if the employee voluntarily authorised deposit in the institution of the employee's choice (8-4-102(2)). Paycard allowed only if the employee has free access to the entire net pay at least once per pay period, or may choose another payment means (8-4-102(2.5)). Checks must be negotiable without discount (8-4-102(1)). Paydays must be posted (8-4-107).

instrument_name: Colorado Wage Act C.R.S. 8-4-109(1) final pay; 8-4-101(14)(a)(III) vacation pay; 8-4-101(14)(b) severance
authority: Colorado General Assembly (text published by CDLE)
figure_or_rule_carried: Discharge (employer volition): wages earned, vested, determinable and unpaid due immediately; if payroll unit not operational, available within 6 hours of the start of its next regular workday, or within 24 hours if the unit is off-site (delivered to work site, local office or last mailing address). Resignation: due on the next regular payday. Unclaimed check mailed after 60 days. Vacation: employer that provides paid vacation must pay on separation all vacation earned and determinable under the agreement (wages, 8-4-101(14)(a)(III)). Severance is not wages (14)(b). Penalty after written demand unpaid 14 days: greater of 2x unpaid wages or 1,000 USD (8-4-109(3)(b)).

instrument_name: Colorado Wage Act C.R.S. 8-4-105 permitted payroll deductions
authority: Colorado General Assembly (text published by CDLE)
figure_or_rule_carried: Only these deductions: (a) required by law (taxes, FICA, garnishments, court orders); (a.5) automatic enrolment retirement contributions; (b) loans, advances, goods/services, equipment under a written enforceable agreement; (c) theft shortage after a police report (refund with interest if no charge within 90 days or acquittal); (d) other deductions authorised by the employee if the authorisation is revocable (insurance, savings, stock, charities, deposits); (e) unreturned money/property of a terminated employee entrusted with it, with notice within 10 calendar days of termination.

instrument_name: Healthy Families and Workplaces Act C.R.S. 8-13.3-403, -404 (text revised Aug 7, 2023)
authority: Colorado General Assembly (text published by CDLE)
figure_or_rule_carried: All employers (since 2022-01-01): 1 hour paid sick leave per 30 hours worked, up to 48 hours/year (employer may front-load); overtime-exempt employees accrue as if 40 h/week (or normal week if shorter); up to 48 unused hours carry forward but use may be capped at 48/year; no payout of unused sick leave on separation (except as retaliation remedy); reinstatement if rehired within 6 months; public health emergency supplement 80 hours (40+ h/week) or 14-day average. Partial: 2023 edition; later amendments (2024-2026 sessions) not checked.

instrument_name: Colorado Wage Withholding Tax Guide (Revised January 2026), Parts 1, 3, 4: account, returns, deposits, W-2 filing
authority: Colorado Department of Revenue (CDOR), Taxation Division
article_or_section: Part 1 (account, W-4 copy rule); Part 3 table 'Filing Frequency and Due Dates'; Part 4 (W-2, DR 1093, DR 0995)
figure_or_rule_carried: Account: register at mybiz.colorado.gov or CR 0100; close via Revenue Online or DR 1108. Filing frequency by annual withholding: < 7,000 quarterly (due last day of month after quarter); 7,000-50,000 monthly (due 15th of following month); >= 50,000 weekly (week Sat-Fri, due 3rd business day after the Friday; EFT mandatory). Monthly/quarterly filers file zero returns; weekly filers need not. Paper return DR 1094. W-2s to employees and to CDOR by January 31; electronic filing to CDOR mandatory if the employer must e-file federal W-2s (10+ W-2s from 2024), via Revenue Online 'Submit Year-End Withholding' (.txt upload, register 5 days before); paper filers send W-2s with DR 1093 annual transmittal; penalty 5-50 USD per W-2 late. W-2c to employee and CDOR. Annual DR 0995 refundable-credit notice to every employee in English plus the language the employer typically uses (paper min 5.5x8.5 in; electronic must carry full text, no bare link). Employer must send CDOR a copy of a W-4 claiming exempt where pay > 200 USD/week and no DR 0004 submitted.

instrument_name: Colorado Wage Withholding Tax Guide (Revised January 2026), Part 2: wages subject to withholding; federal conformity; OBBBA overtime
authority: Colorado Department of Revenue (CDOR), Taxation Division
article_or_section: Part 2 'Wages', 'Overtime compensation', 'Exempt wages', table 'Exempt Wages for Nonresident Employees'
figure_or_rule_carried: Wages subject to CO withholding = wages subject to federal withholding (salaries, vacation, bonuses, commissions, fringe benefits); wages exempt from federal withholding are generally exempt from CO withholding (conformity; no state-specific departure listed for 401(k)/125/HSA/transit/GTL). Departure: overtime compensation that may be exempted from federal withholding under the One Big Beautiful Bill Act remains subject to CO withholding (handled through DR 0004 Worksheet 1). Nonresident exemptions: rail carrier (49 USC 11502), air carrier with no more than 50% of pay earned in CO (49 USC 40116(f)), motor carrier (49 USC 14503(a)), military pay (50 USC 4001(b)), military spouse (50 USC 4001(c)), telecommuters for work performed outside CO.

instrument_name: CDLE FAMLI Division, FAMLI Business Brief of 2026-09-30 (official employer bulletin)
authority: Colorado Department of Labor and Employment, Family & Medical Leave Insurance Division
article_or_section: Employer Actions & Deadlines; Heads-up: 2027 Premium Rate; Portal Report; Beyond FAMLI
figure_or_rule_carried: FAMLI premium 2027 = 0.86% of wages (down from 0.88% in 2026), effective 2027-01-01. Quarterly FAMLI wage reports and premiums filed in My FAMLI+ Employer, Q3 2026 due 2026-10-31 (quarter-end + 1 month); file specifications and Wage Report API specifications published; from 2026-10-01 bulk wage files may carry ITINs for employees without SSN; private-plan (SIPP) employers file quarterly administrative reports by email; FAMLI Program Notice must be posted/provided. Employees may top-off FAMLI benefits with accrued PTO/sick leave up to average weekly wage. HFWA 1h/30h up to 48h restated. Colorado SecureSavings: employers without a plan register or certify exemption. 2027 employer/employee split not stated (statute default 50/50: not read here).

instrument_name: Colorado Judicial Branch Form 26 SC, Writ of Continuing Garnishment (R: 1/22), incl. Calculation of the Amount of Exempt Earnings and Explanation of Wage Garnishment
article_or_section: Notice to Garnishee a-f; Calculation; Exemption Chart; Explanation (implements C.R.S. 13-54-104 and 13-54.5)
figure_or_rule_carried: Disposable earnings = gross less deductions required by law (income taxes, FICA) AND employer-provided health insurance withheld (CO departure from CCPA). Amount exempt = greater of 80% of disposable earnings or 40x (weekly) / 80x (bi-weekly) / 86.67x (semi-monthly) / 173.3x (monthly) the minimum hourly wage, where minimum hourly wage = state or federal, whichever greater; i.e. garnish the lesser of 20% of disposable earnings or the excess over 40x minimum wage (weekly). Wage/income assignments (support) in the period are deducted first; a writ for support or prior continuing writ takes priority and the new writ starts after it terminates. Garnishee pays from the first pay date at least 21 days after service. Tips excluded from 'earnings' on this form. 2026 weekly floor derived: 40 x 15.16 = 606.40 USD. Statute text 13-54-104 itself not read on an official host (CRS official host is LexisNexis, gated).

instrument_name: City and County of Denver, Department of Finance news release 'Denver Local Minimum Wage Adjusts to $19.29 per Hour for 2026' (D.R.M.C. Chapter 58, Art. 16)
authority: City and County of Denver, Department of Finance (enforcement: Denver Labor, Office of the Auditor)
figure_or_rule_carried: Denver local minimum wage 19.29 USD/h from 2026-01-01 (2025: 18.81); tipped food and beverage workers 16.27 USD/h provided at least 3.02 USD actual tips (tip credit 3.02). Indexed annually by CPI-W Denver-Aurora-Lakewood, first half of current year vs first half of prior year; 2026 step 2.56%. Derivation: 18.81 x 1.0256 = 19.2915 -> 19.29; 19.29 - 3.02 = 16.27. Changes take effect 1 January (state law). Enforced by Denver Labor (Auditor). Retrieved via Wayback (denvergov.org returns a bot-rejection page to scripts).

instrument_name: DR 0004, 2026 Colorado Employee Withholding Certificate (rev. 10/29/25), with Worksheet 1, Table 1 Standard Allowance, Table 2 Child Tax Credit Allowance and Line 3 worksheet
article_or_section: Line 2 Annual Withholding Allowance; Table 1; Worksheet 1 lines 1-5 (3b qualified overtime); Table 2; Line 3 worksheet (x 4.40%)
figure_or_rule_carried: DR 0004 is optional (W-4 alone suffices; if line 2 blank, employer uses an amount based on the W-4 per DR 1098). Table 1 Standard Allowance by W-4 Step 1(c) status and number of jobs: Single/MFS 14,000 (1 job) / 7,000 (2) / 4,500 (3) / 3,500 (4+); Head of household 22,000 / 11,000 / 7,500 / 5,500; MFJ/QSS 30,000 / 15,000 / 10,000 / 7,500 (row/column alignment confirmed on pdftotext -raw extraction). Worksheet 1 removes from federal additional deductions (W-4 Step 4(b)) the qualified overtime deduction (line 3b) and state income tax (3c): OBBBA overtime deduction not allowed for CO withholding. Line 3 additional withholding computed at 4.40%. Table 2 child tax credit allowance by status and income.

instrument_name: CDOR Year-End W-2 XLSX Info Return Template (2026 filing season) and instructions page (Revenue Online upload)
article_or_section: Template tabs Employer Info (RE), Employee Info (RS), Instructions; Withholding Submitter Access steps 1-5
figure_or_rule_carried: Alternative electronic W-2 submission for employers with 10-100 employees required to e-file for tax year 2026 (filed in calendar 2027): XLSX template uploaded in Revenue Online (besides the .txt file route). Required RE fields: tax year, employer name, federal ID type (1 EIN, 2 SSN, 3 ITIN, 4 ATIN), EIN (9 digits, no dashes), street, city, state, ZIP. Required RS fields: employer ID type and EIN, employee first/last name, SSN (9 digits; 999999999 if none; CO withholding required if no valid TIN), address, city, state, ZIP, box 1, box 2, box 15 state, box 16 state wages, box 17 state tax; optional local boxes 18-20, second state, email, date first employed, separation date, weeks worked, SUI wages. Currency 0..999,999,999.99. Withholding Submitter Access required first (IRS TIN matching; third-party submitters register once under own FEIN).

instrument_name: US DOL OUI Comparison of State Unemployment Insurance Laws 2023, Chapter 1 Coverage, Tables 1-1 to 1-9 (Colorado entries)
authority: US Department of Labor, Employment and Training Administration, Office of Unemployment Insurance
figure_or_rule_carried: Colorado UI coverage (2023 edition; 2025/2026 editions return 404): CO is not listed in Table 1-1 (employer definition), 1-2 (agricultural) or 1-3 (domestic), so it follows the FUTA thresholds: employer 20 weeks / 1,500 USD quarter; agricultural 10 workers in 20 weeks or 20,000 USD quarter; domestic 1,000 USD in a quarter. Table 1-5: CO excludes insurance agents on commission, real-estate agents on commission, casual labor not in the course of the employer's business, and part-time service for nonprofits exempt from federal income tax. Table 1-6: CO excludes students working for schools (not student nurses/interns). CO not listed in Table 1-7 (corporate officers special rule). Partial: 2023 edition; C.R.S. 8-70-103/8-70-140 text not read (official CRS host is LexisNexis).

instrument_name: City of Greenwood Village, Occupational Privilege Tax (OPT) page
authority: City of Greenwood Village, Taxpayer Services
article_or_section: Tax Portions; How to Remit; Employees with Multiple Employers; PEO
figure_or_rule_carried: Greenwood Village OPT (since 1980-01-01): employee portion 2 USD/month withheld + employer portion 2 USD/month (total 4), both when 250 USD or more is earned in a calendar month in the Village; owners/partners/officers earning under 250 pay only the employer portion. OPT license required for every business located in the Village (one-time 10 USD fee; construction/temp-placement employers working long term may also need one). Employer reports and remits both portions online (Xpress Bill Pay). Multiple OPT cities: payable to the city where the employee worked the most; only the primary employer withholds. PEO clients still licensed. Separate city return (T4 element). Replaces, for this city only, the tier-C figure in US-COP7-006 (which still carries Sheridan).

instrument_name: City of Glendale (CO), Occupational Privilege Tax page
article_or_section: OPT page; links to OPT ordinance and monthly/quarterly/annual returns
figure_or_rule_carried: Glendale OPT ('head tax'): employees working within Glendale who earn more than 750 USD in a calendar month pay 5 USD/month, matched by employer 5 USD (total 10). Self-employed, owners, partners, officers not paid salary/commission pay only the employer portion. Monthly, quarterly and annual OPT returns exist (frequency rule in the ordinance, not read). Separate city return (T4 element). Replaces, for this city only, the tier-C figure in US-COP7-006 (which still carries Sheridan).
